clue.text: Many are the hours misused in school

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

indicators.note: words that are misused are put to the wrong purpose, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a great many lesson hours are wasted at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges ARE THE HOURS into HARTERHOUSE, placed after C. CHARTERHOUSE is a famous English public (private boarding) school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is a well-known independent boarding school, so it is an example of a school.

clue.text: The spiteful woman's regard for a gem

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful woman, and the possessive gives CAT'S
to regard is to eye, look at

explanation.surface: A catty woman gazes enviously at someone else's jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-eye is a gemstone, usually chrysoberyl, showing a narrow band of reflected light.

clue.text: A crop -it could be fruit

indicators.note: the letters could be something else when shuffled into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders whether a crop might turn out to be fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a soft orange stone fruit.

clue.text: On reflection, not the place for the captain in town

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word not is read backwards

parts.note: a ship's captain commands from the bridge

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a sailor decides town is no place for a ship's master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns NOT into TON. TONBRIDGE is a town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a market town in Kent, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Periods of relaxation needed by snooker-players

explanation.surface: Snooker players need breaks between frames.
explanation.definitionFit: Rests are pauses from work; in snooker a rest is the cue support used for awkward shots.

clue.text: Round enclosure to display out-of-doors

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
a pen is an enclosure for animals
to air something is to display or show it

explanation.surface: A circular pen is built to show off livestock outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something happening outside, under the sky rather than indoors.

clue.text: Singers, taking pains or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Vocalists either take trouble over their art or they don't.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani is the Italian plural of soprano, the highest female singing voices.

clue.text: Stretchers for supple crews?

parts.note: supple and elastic both mean flexible, able to stretch
bands are groups or crews of people

explanation.surface: A rowing coach seeks stretching gear for flexible teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretchers' suggests stretcher-bearers or rowing footrests; here it means things that stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber loops that stretch round objects to hold them, hence playful things that stretch.

clue.text: There's more behind an old palace

parts.note: behind can mean late, so more behind is later

explanation.surface: Someone explains there's an extra building behind a historic royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lateran is the ancient papal palace in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran Palace in Rome was the residence of the popes for centuries, an old palace indeed.

clue.text: A feature of the church — up to a point

definitions.text: A feature of the church — up to a point

parts.words: A feature of the church — up to a point
parts.note: seems to say a church feature only partly; really a tall church tower rising to a pointed tip

explanation.surface: Something is a church feature, though only to a certain degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering tower on a church rises to a point at the top.

clue.text: Ideal jewelry for the continuity girl

definitions.text: Ideal jewelry for the continuity girl

parts.words: Ideal jewelry for the continuity girl
parts.note: a film continuity assistant would love a ring symbolising never-ending time

explanation.surface: A gift suggestion for the film crew member who checks continuity.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring set with a continuous band of stones, symbolising endless love, suits someone concerned with continuity.

clue.text: A painter's short underwear

explanation.surface: An artist wears skimpy undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Spencer was an English painter; a spencer is also a short woollen undervest or close-fitting jacket.

clue.text: The main road?

parts.note: main is an old word for the open sea, so a road on the main is a shipping route

explanation.surface: Someone asks which is the principal highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A recognised route for ships across the ocean, the main being a poetic word for the sea.

clue.text: It holds a writer back, which is silly

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, so the second goes within the first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going back means the word for a writer is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is something you write with

explanation.surface: A thing restrains an author, and that is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a writer' looks like an author but is the pen, turned round by 'back' and held inside 'It'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or foolishly unsuitable.

clue.text: One's tired out, so leaving

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is exhausted, so they're going home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ONES TIRED; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is the act of abandoning someone or a post, a noun for leaving.

clue.text: A row between holy men — most surprising!

indicators.note: one piece sits between the two parts of another

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, and two holy men give two of them
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: A quarrel between two clergymen is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel, which suits the surface; it is a line, as of mountains, held 'between' the two saints.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangest is the superlative of strange, meaning the most unusual or unexpected.

clue.text: Boycott support for the beast

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as a union might
to bear is to support or carry

explanation.surface: Someone calls for a boycott in support of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The black bear is a North American or Asian species of the animal.

clue.text: They get put on

parts.note: sounds like clothes or acts; really material added at the end of a book

explanation.surface: Things like clothes or theatre shows that are put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are additions appended to a text, items added on.

clue.text: A woolly-thinking manual worker

parts.note: seems a muddled labourer; really someone working wool by hand with needles

explanation.surface: A labourer whose ideas are confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes garments from yarn by hand, thinking about wool as they work.

clue.text: Patent covering tin-opener

parts.note: over can mean covering, lying on top of

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone takes out a patent on a lid for a can opener.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent can mean obvious or open, which is the sense of overt.

clue.text: Last longer in general without wearying

indicators.note: the answer sits in the general run of the following words, spanning the join between them

explanation.surface: Someone claims a thing lasts longer, in general, without wearing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like an army officer, but 'in general' just says the letters run on inside the closing words.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear is to last longer than something, enduring beyond it.

clue.text: Eastern conqueror — he put people out

parts.note: a victor is a conqueror

explanation.surface: A conqueror from the East drove people from their homes.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor expels tenants from a property.

clue.text: Being agreeable, though half-asleep

explanation.surface: Someone agrees along with everything while dozing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding signals assent, and nodding off is drifting into sleep.

clue.text: Eat too much Cheddar for example

explanation.surface: Someone overindulges in cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to overeat; Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England.

clue.text: The French artist is smarter

explanation.surface: A painter from France is better dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Marc Nattier was an 18th-century French portraitist; nattier means neater or better dressed.

clue.text: A politician finds his constituents aren't so bad

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician discovers the voters in their constituency aren't so terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges ARENTSO, the apostrophe ignored; 'constituents' hints at the letters being parts of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, a kind of politician.

clue.text: The football team's right to occupy flat

indicators.note: these letters occupy the word for flat, sitting inside it

parts.note: flat means level or even
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football club claims the right to live in a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupy' puts R and TO inside the word for flat. Everton is a football club from Liverpool, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League club from Liverpool, an example of a football team.

clue.text: Just the thing for those seeking capital growth!

definitions.text: Just the thing for those seeking capital growth!

parts.words: Just the thing for those seeking capital growth!
parts.note: sounds like investment advice; capital here is the head, and growth is of hair

explanation.surface: An investment tip for those hoping their money will grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic sold to bald people to make their scalp sprout again.
